To: docs/climate-programme/border-revenues-launch/handover
Replying to: none
Cc: none
Subject: Thursday launch handover — draft for Inês

Inês,

Thank you for taking Thursday on. I’m sorry to leave you with the figure 3 correction at this stage, and for the extra work it creates. The 2.1 figure was my mistake, not yours. If anyone asks, please say that plainly.

I trust you completely with the launch. You know the paper as well as I do, and you ran the annex B sensitivity work yourself. You’re ready for the questions and for the room. And remember Lisbon, when the projector died during my panel: you rescued the whole thing. You’re better live than you think.

## First: fix the materials and the press line

The corrected PDF, v7, is on the drive. It has the right 2030 LDC-relevant revenue estimate: **EUR 1.4 billion, not EUR 2.1 billion**. The conclusion is unchanged, but the headline number is not.

1. **Correct the slide deck before it is presented.** Deck v4 still has the old figure on slides 6 and 9. Update both using the corrected number and check the chart labels, speaker notes and any other references to 2.1. Save a clearly named final version in the launch folder. Please check it against PDF v7, especially pages 3, 14 and 15.

2. **Coordinate with Hanna on the press release today.** The release sent to 34 Brussels contacts on Friday is still under embargo until Thursday 10:00 CET and contains the old number. Hanna should send a corrected version to the same contacts before the embargo lifts, making clear that this corrects the 2030 estimate. Please agree the wording and distribution with her, and check what she wants to do about the two journalists who requested background calls. If Hanna needs a senior name to sign off the corrected release, Geert knows I’m away and can do that.

3. **Use one consistent line everywhere:** the corrected estimate is EUR 1.4 billion; the earlier 2.1 figure was an error in my calculation, not Inês’s. Don’t let the old number survive in slides, press materials or answers.

## Press calls and launch-day running order

Hanna had pencilled in background calls with a trade newsletter and a Belgian daily for Wednesday at 14:00 and 15:00, 20 minutes each. Please confirm with her whether those calls are still happening and who will take them. If you do, use the corrected figure and make sure the journalists have the corrected release. Don’t speculate beyond the paper or imply the conclusion has changed.

The event is Thursday 26 November at the European Parliament, Altiero Spinelli building. Guests need to be at the security entrance by **12:00**; Tomás Reyes is collecting badges, and he needs our final names by **Wednesday at 12:00**. Please confirm the team’s names to him in time. Light lunch is outside the room from 12:00.

The MEP’s vote has changed the timings from the original run of show. The current sequence is:

- **12:30** welcome from MEP Katarina Lindqvist (5 minutes)
- **12:35** your presentation (15 minutes)
- **12:50** panel with Dr. Abena Owusu-Mensah, Florian Kessler and you, moderated by Lindqvist
- Lindqvist needs to leave at **13:30** and would like to take at least two questions before she goes
- **13:40** Q&A; **14:00** close

Please confirm any remaining practical details with Tomás. Abena’s remote link is in the calendar invite; she tested it and it worked. It’s still worth checking the connection and having a fallback plan in case the room technology misbehaves.

## Handling the panel

Kessler is likely to focus on the assumption that downstream steel users can pass through 80% of the border cost, and may raise resource shuffling. Don’t let the 80% figure set the tone for the whole discussion. Acknowledge that it is the central case, then explain the sensitivity results directly: the effect holds at 60% pass-through and weakens at 40%. You ran those annex B scenarios, so you can speak to them with confidence. Don’t be defensive; be clear about what the analysis does and does not show.

On resource shuffling, the paper recognises it as a risk in section 5.2 and recommends the Commission’s monitoring report. Say that openly. Keep the discussion anchored in the paper’s findings and the LDC relevance, rather than letting one challenge become the whole event.

## On the day

You have the speaker notes I left in the deck. Once the corrected deck is ready, do one final run-through against the shortened 15-minute slot and make sure the opening and headline number are unambiguous. During the panel, it’s fine to take a beat before answering and to bring the conversation back to the evidence. You don’t need to perform certainty about things the paper doesn’t claim.

Lucy Tran from the Halvorsen Foundation is attending with a colleague. She’ll need two event photos and attendance numbers for her grant report by 4 December. Please arrange for someone to take a couple of usable photos and note the final attendance count; don’t let that become another last-minute task.

My father is ill; I’m with my family. You can call me, but after 9 tomorrow I may not pick up. Please don’t feel you need to wait for me to make decisions you’re equipped to make.

I’m sorry again for the late correction and the extra load. I know you’ll handle this well, and I trust you completely.
